raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This ports the Kimi-K3 specialized decode ([#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683), MI355X) to gfx942, validated on MI325X. The kernels run on any gfx942 with 304 CUs. But Kimi-K3 at TP8 holds 199.89 GiB of weights a rank (the same with the kernels off and on), more than an MI300X's 192 GB. So MI300X can't serve it either way. 

It keeps the same folder, the same switch (`additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}`), and the same refusals, per-step plan, layer mode and fail-stop.

## Validation

All runs are on 8x MI325X (gfx942, 304 CUs).

- **pytest** `tests/models/kimi_k3`: 343 passed, 200 skipped, 0 failed. This includes:
  - K1 and K2 (TP8) against vLLM's ops at widths 8 / 6 / 4 / 2. Width 6 is the K2 build with the most LDS.
  - A CUDA graph of K2 at each width, replayed 300 times bit for bit.
  - A stalled rank.
  - The served fail-stop test (dummy 8 layers, TP8: requests are served, then all 8 ranks give up at the same step and the server exits).
  - These ran before the rebase onto current `main`. The rebase changed none of the kernel or numerics files. After it, `test_runtime.py`, now with upstream's MoRIIO tests, gives 56 passed.
- **ISA:** gfx950 builds are 28/28 byte-identical to `main`. gfx942 builds use no private memory and spill no VGPRs; the peak LDS is 62,496 B of 65,536 (K2, width 6).
- **Startup refusal:** one deployment with TP4, the V1 model runner, no speculative decoding, gfx942 without the int4 flag and `ARCH=gfx950` gives the same `ValueError` on every rank, listing all five reasons. `decode_backend="fast"` is rejected.
- **pre-commit** (including mypy): passes.

### Performance

`vllm bench serve`, 3 seeds (0/1/2) a cell, 8 prompts per concurrency slot a seed, the off and on servers otherwise identical (serving flags under Details). The random rows use 1024 output tokens with `ignore_eos` and synthetic rejection sampling. Acceptance length 3.84 at k=7 is the drafter's measured rate. At k=3 and k=1 it is 1.0 (every draft rejected), so TPOT there is the time of one decode step. The ShareGPT row uses block rejection, so drafts are accepted as they really are: about 2.3 tokens a step on both sides (off 2.45 / 2.22 / 2.34, on 2.47 / 2.20 / 2.27). Each cell is the mean over seeds. In every row the kernels serve, the off and on TPOT ranges over the 3 seeds do not overlap.

| config | TTFT p50 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | TPOT p90 (ms) | output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1, k=7, random 8k | 1097 → 1098 (+0.1%) | 7.85 → **6.40 (−18.5%)** | 7.91 → 6.55 (−17.2%) | 112.3 → **133.8 (+19.2%)** |
| c1, k=7, random 64k | 8458 → 8448 (−0.1%) | 10.71 → 9.28 (−13.3%) | 10.79 → 9.38 (−13.0%) | 52.9 → 57.3 (+8.3%) |
| c1, k=7, ShareGPT, real acceptance | 184 → 178 (−3.1%) | 13.26 → **10.53 (−20.6%)** | 18.12 → 14.40 (−20.6%) | 77.1 → **92.6 (+20.0%)** |
| c2, k=3, random 8k | 1655 → 1648 (−0.4%) | 28.86 → 24.06 (−16.6%) | 29.43 → 24.62 (−16.4%) | 65.7 → 78.2 (+19.0%) |
| c4, k=1, random 8k | 3901 → 3892 (−0.2%) | 28.68 → 24.54 (−14.4%) | 31.25 → 27.07 (−13.4%) | 123.8 → 142.1 (+14.8%) |
| c8, k=1, random 8k (16 rows: vLLM's decode) | 4893 → 4892 (−0.0%) | 35.85 → 35.78 (−0.2%) | 39.38 → 39.33 (−0.1%) | 196.2 → 196.7 (+0.3%) |

At 64k the kernels save the same TPOT as at 8k (1.43 vs 1.45 ms). The relative gain is smaller only because the MLA layers' attention, which stays on vLLM's path (the kernels take only those layers' FFN), reads a longer context. The servers log `Kimi-K3 specialized decode: 92 layers, widths [8], 30 builds` at k=7, `widths [4, 8], 60 builds` at k=3 and `widths [2, 4, 6, 8], 120 builds` at k=1.

### Accuracy

Every config fuses every decode step: conc x (k+1) <= 8, and the padded c3 replays the 4-request graph.

| eval | config | off | on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 q | c1, k=7 | 0.9575 | 0.9545 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c4, k=1 | 0.9522 | 0.9568 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, padded replays | c3, k=1 | 0.9553 | 0.9538 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c2, k=3 | 0.9538 | 0.9591 |
| AIME24 + AIME25 (60 q), avg@4, T=1.0, top_p 0.95, 60K tokens | c4, k=1 | 0.9458 | 0.9333 |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 q, CoT, 0-shot), T=1.0, top_p 0.95, 60K tokens | c4, k=1 | 0.8939 | 0.8788 |
| NIAH single_1 / single_2 / multikey_1 @ 8k, 100 each | c4, k=1 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 |
| NIAH single_1 / multikey_2 / multikey_3 @ 32k / 128k / 256k, 20 each | c1, k=7 | | 1.00 (all) |

GSM8K strict-match equals flexible-extract in every cell (stderr 0.0055 to 0.0059). Paired GSM8K, counting questions right only with the kernels on vs only with them off (exact McNemar):

- c1/k7: 7 vs 11, p = 0.48.
- c4/k1: 14 vs 8, p = 0.29.
- c3/k1: 12 vs 14, p = 0.85.
- c2/k3: 15 vs 8, p = 0.21.

AIME per repeat: off 0.900 / 1.000 / 0.933 / 0.950, on 0.917 / 0.933 / 0.933 / 0.950. No response was truncated. Per problem over the 4 repeats, 6 problems score higher with the kernels on and 7 with them off.

GPQA-Diamond is lm-eval's `gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot` with flexible-extract (stderr 0.022 / 0.023), and both sides get the same shuffled choices. Paired, 6 questions are right only with the kernels on and 9 only with them off (exact McNemar p = 0.61); 15 are wrong on both. Each side has 3 empty answers that spent the whole 60K budget thinking, 2 of them on the same questions. Strict-match is 0 on both sides, because Kimi-K3 boxes its answer instead of writing "The answer is".

## Details

**Duplicate check:** no other open PR ports the K3 specialized decode to gfx942. [#61498](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61498) is MI355X only. 

**What changes on gfx942:**

- `mono/common/arch.py` picks the target the way FlyDSL does (`ARCH`, else the GPU), and sets the LDS size: 64 KB instead of 160 KB.
- **K1:** in_proj streams x a K window at a time (`stage_gemv_pair`). The next window loads under the current window's MFMAs.
- **K2:**
  - The routed experts read vLLM's packed-int4 requant in place (aiter's a16wi4 layout, `mono/common/i4.py`). gfx942 has no MXFP4 MFMA, so the latent and the intermediate stay bf16, staged in K phases / K slices.
  - The dequant reproduces aiter's gfx942 int4 dequant bit for bit.
  - The 16x16x32 bf16 MFMA runs as two 16x16x16, and `shuffle_xor` replaces the permlane swaps.
- **Runtime:**
  - Startup refuses three things:
    - gfx942 without the int4 flag;
    - any GPU with fewer CUs than the 256 CTAs (an MI325X has 304, and the rest idle);
    - an `ARCH` environment variable that differs from the GPU, which would make FlyDSL build the kernels for another GPU than the one the checks and vLLM's MoE follow.
  - The weight guard checks the int4 experts' shape, dtype, shuffle and scale layout.
- The gfx950 code paths are unchanged.

**Serving on gfx942:** these constraints come from vLLM's MLA backends, not from this change:

- The DSpark draft is non-causal. `ROCM_AITER_MLA` has no gfx942 non-causal kernel, and `TRITON_MLA` refuses non-causal attention with DCP. So gfx942 runs DCP 1 with `"attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA"` for the draft.
- AITER's gfx942 fp8 MLA decode takes at most 4 query rows (k=7 needs 8), so the KV cache is bf16.

The README documents this, together with the `--quantization-config` flag.

```
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 8 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'
```

**CI:** a new `mi300_1` step runs `tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode` on one MI300 (K1 and the warm-up compiles). There is no 8-GPU MI300 pool, so the TP8 K2 and served tests skip in CI and were run locally (above).

**Complexity:** about 1,000 lines of kernel code, almost all of it the gfx942 int4 / LDS-windowed variants in `moe.py`, `gemv.py`, `kda.py` and `i4.py`, each behind `GFX942`.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude, in Cursor).

+"""The GPU architecture the mono kernels are compiled for.
+
+FlyDSL compiles for the architecture in the ARCH environment variable, and
+otherwise for the GPU it finds. The kernels were written for gfx950 (MI355X).
+gfx942 (MI300X, MI325X) has 64 KB of LDS a CU instead of 160 KB, and lacks the
+scaled f8f6f4 MFMA, the 16x16x32 bf16 MFMA, v_permlane16_swap /

+``GFX942`` and take another code path there; the gfx950 code is unchanged.
+
+Only kernel modules import this one: the runtime (``plan`` included) must import
+without FlyDSL, as the CPU tests do.
+"""
+
+import os
+
+from flydsl.runtime.device import get_rocm_arch
+
+
+def target_arch() -> str:
+    """The architecture FlyDSL compiles for, as FlyDSL's ROCm backend picks it."""
+    arch = os.environ.get("ARCH") or get_rocm_arch()
+    return arch.lower().split(":")[0]
+

+"""Packed-int4 expert weights (gfx942): the layout vLLM leaves K3's MXFP4 experts
+in on gfx942 (``Mxfp4MoEMethod._setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942``: requantized by
+``per_1x32_i4_quant``, ``shuffle_weight(16, 16)``, ``pack_int8_to_packed_int4``,
+scales by ``shuffle_scale_for_int4``) and aiter's a16wi4 dequant of it.
+
+A weight [E, N, K] is 16-row groups of 64-K blocks of 512 B. Lane l's 8 B of a
+block (byte 8 l) are row l % 16's K 16 (l / 16) .. + 15: two dwords of eight
+nibbles, byte j holding K j (low nibble) and K j + 4 (high). The scales (a
+group of 32 K) are bf16 [E, K / 64, N, 2]: dword (k0, n) holds row n's groups
+2 k0 (low half) and 2 k0 + 1 (high), lane l's the half (l / 16) // 2.
+
+The MFMA's other operand is read at the same K (16 bf16 a lane a block), so a
+block is two ``mfma_bf16`` (four 16x16x16) of ``dequant``'s two v8bf16.
+"""
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
+from flydsl._mlir.dialects import llvm
+from flydsl.expr import rocdl
+from flydsl.expr.typing import T
+
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.ops import CM_NT
+
+BLOCK_K = 64
+GROUP = 32
+
+
+def group_dw(k):
+    """Dwords of a 16-row group of a K = ``k`` weight."""
+    return 2 * k
+
+
+def expert_dw(n, k):
+    """Dwords of one expert's [n, k] weight."""
+    return n * k // 8
+
+
+def block_load(r_w, base, blk, lane):
+    """A lane's dwordx2 of 64-K block ``blk`` of the 16-row group at dword
+    ``base``. Nontemporal: a weight a step reads once."""
+    return fx.Vector(
+        bo.buffer_load(
+            r_w, base + blk * 128 + 2 * lane, vec_width=2, dtype=T.i32,
+            cache_modifier=CM_NT,
+        )
+    )  # fmt: skip
+
+
+def scale_word(r_s, e, row, blk, n, k):
+    """The scale dword of (expert e, weight row ``row``, 64-K block ``blk``) of
+    an [n, k] weight."""
+    return fx.Int32(
+        bo.buffer_load(
+            r_s, (e * (k // BLOCK_K) + blk) * n + row, vec_width=1, dtype=T.i32
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def lane_scale(word, lane):
+    """The f32 group scale of this lane's 16 K in a scale dword."""
+    hi = (lane // 16) >= 2
+    return hi.select(word & fx.Int32(-65536), word << 16).bitcast(fx.Float32)
+
+
+def _nibbles_bf16x8(raw, eff2):
+    """Eight int4 of ``raw`` (K j low, K j + 4 high) times ``eff2`` / 16 (a pair
+    a v_pk_mul_f32) -> v8bf16 K 0 .. 7, by high-16 truncation (a v_perm_b32 a
+    pair): aiter's gfx942 ``_int4_nibble_to_bf16x8(old_pack=True)`` bit for
+    bit."""
+    odd = fx.Int32(raw).shrui(fx.Int32(4))
+    f = [rocdl.cvt_off_f32_i4(fx.Int32(raw).ir_value(), byte_sel=j) for j in range(4)]
+    f += [rocdl.cvt_off_f32_i4(odd.ir_value(), byte_sel=j) for j in range(4)]
+    hi16 = fx.Int32(0x07060302)  # perm_b32(hi_w, lo_w): their high halves
+    words = []
+    for i in range(4):
+        p = fx.Vector.from_elements(f[2 * i : 2 * i + 2], fx.Float32) * eff2
+        lo_w, hi_w = p[0].bitcast(fx.Int32), p[1].bitcast(fx.Int32)
+        words.append(fx.Int32(rocdl.perm_b32(hi_w, lo_w, hi16)))
+    return fx.Vector.from_elements(words, fx.Int32).bitcast(fx.BFloat16)
+
+
+def dequant(raw2, scale):
+    """A lane's block dwordx2 with its f32 group scale -> (v8bf16 K 0 .. 7,
+    v8bf16 K 8 .. 15) of its 16."""
+    eff = scale * fx.Float32(16.0)
+    # both halves defined: a splat pair's undefined high half makes the waitcnt
+    # pass wait on the load last written to that register (a prefetch)
+    hi = fx.Float32(
+        llvm.call_intrinsic(T.f32, "llvm.arithmetic.fence", [eff.ir_value()], [], [])
+    )
+    eff2 = fx.Vector.from_elements([eff, hi], fx.Float32)
+    return _nibbles_bf16x8(raw2[0], eff2), _nibbles_bf16x8(raw2[1], eff2)

+            s.numel() != E * n * (k // i4.GROUP)
+            or s.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+            or not s.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            reasons.append(
+                f"{p}: {name} scales {s.numel()} {s.dtype}, kernel reads"
+                f" contiguous {E * n * (k // i4.GROUP)} {torch.bfloat16}"
+            )
+    return reasons
+
+
 def cache_reasons(caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
     """Every KDA layer's (conv, recurrent) state as K1 reads them; every MLA
     layer's fp8 cache, rows of 576 bytes (the blocks may be strided)."""
